connections.why: Both AS 1 sections develop close analysis of literary and dramatic methods
Skills of analysing and comparing poems carry forward to pre-1900 poetry at A2
Confident analysis of studied poems prepares students to tackle unseen poems
Both A2 2 sections demand independent reading of poetic method and meaning
Analysing modern drama builds the dramatic-methods skills applied to Shakespeare
Reading a modern play develops the awareness of genre needed for Shakespeare
Comparing tragic and comic conventions sharpens understanding of genre
Problem plays blur comic conventions, deepening genre awareness
The last plays reshape tragic patterns into reconciliation and romance
Studying a pre-1900 novel builds the prose-analysis skills used in the NEA
Both require reading earlier texts within their distinct historical contexts
Comparing texts and exploring context underpins both the NEA and A2 poetry
Context and authorial method are assessed across both AS units
Exploring how writers shape meaning extends from drama to the comparative essay
